title.en: Burnham calls for ‘more open’ public debate about defence spending – UK politics live

summary.zh: 一位重要的工党政治家呼吁就英国的国防开支进行更公开的公众辩论，并阐述了外交政策原则，他将作为下一任工党领袖在无竞争的情况下当选。

Yahweh's vision in Isaiah 2:4 encourages us to imagine a future where military might is transformed into tools for peace and prosperity. Such discussions are vital for discerning how best to contribute to a world where resources serve human flourishing rather...
reflection.zh: 呼吁就国防开支进行公开辩论，促使我们思考国家如何优先分配资源。雅伟在以赛亚书2:4中的愿景鼓励我们构想一个未来，军事力量转化为和平与繁荣的工具。这样的讨论对于辨明如何最好地为一个资源服务于人类繁荣而非冲突的世界做出贡献至关重要。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

Yahweh's word encourages us to act not from selfish ambition or conceit, but with humility, considering others more significant. This perspective calls political actors to prioritize genuine service and the well-being of the community...

verse.textEn: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.
verse.textZh: 凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。

body.en: The plane that French team used after match with Paraguay flew 44 deportation-related flights this year alone The French men’s national soccer team, whose star Kylian Mbappé is one of the world’s most outspoken athletes against far-right politicians, has been using a charter airplane company that is at the heart of the Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign. Images of the team posted on social media and flight tracking data show the French team have used Global Crossing Airlines (GlobalX) for at least three domestic flights between their World Cup games and base camp in Boston. That same airline charter company has operated more than half of ICE’s removal flights in 2024 and 2025. Continue reading...

Yahweh's ancient command reminds us that how we treat foreigners reflects our deepest values, urging us to extend the same love and dignity we desire for ourselves. It challenges us to consider the systems we support, even indirectly,...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了为正义公开倡导与机构实际选择之间的张力。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，如何对待寄居者反映了我们最深层的价值观，敦促我们以对待本地人的爱和尊严来对待他们。它挑战我们思考我们所支持的系统，即使是间接支持，以及它们对最脆弱群体的影响。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.

title.en: International court tells BBC of breakthrough in Sudan war crimes probe
title.zh: 国际法院向BBC透露苏丹战争罪调查取得突破

summary.en: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has announced a significant development in its investigation into alleged war crimes committed in Darfur over the past three years.
summary.zh: 国际刑事法院（ICC）宣布，其对过去三年在达尔富尔地区犯下的战争罪行指控的调查取得了重大进展。

body.en:
The International Criminal Court (ICC) has "concrete evidence" linking leaders of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to recent war crimes in the Sudanese region of Darfur, the ICC's deputy chief prosecutor says.

Nazhat Shameem Khan told the BBC the ICC had reached a "breakthrough" in its investigation into the massacres of civilians in the cities of el-Fasher and el-Geneina.

"It may take time for justice to develop, to be brought to the court, but we will get there," Khan said, adding that RSF leaders have also been linked to crimes against humanity.

The siege and takeover of el-Fasher marked one of the bloodiest episodes in the ongoing war between the RSF and Sudan's army.

More than 6,000 people were killed in el-Fasher as the RSF seized the city in October last year, the United Nations says, while the paramilitary group is accused of carrying out a similar massacre in el-Geneina .

The group has repeatedly denied carrying out widespread killings anywhere in Darfur.

A UN fact-finding mission report released on Wednesday also found evidence of widespread atrocities in Sudan's conflict by both the army and the RSF.

It said RSF fighters were responsible for most of the systematic attacks on civilians, particularly in Darfur, where people were targeted based on ethnic grounds, which "may amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity".

RSF fighters and affiliated groups have also committed sexual abuses including rape, gang rape, sexual slavery, and other forms of abuses when they captured el-Fasher last year, according to the UN fact-finding mission.

Speaking to the BBC about the ICC's investigation, Khan said: "We have now found concrete evidence that links what is happening on the ground through linkage evidence to specific persons in leadership mode."

However, she did not give a timeline on when charges might be brought against those responsible for the atrocities in the war, which began in April 2023.

"But we can say that progress has been significant and that we have achieved a breakthrough."

The ICC, based in the Dutch city of The Hague, is a global court with the power to bring prosecutions for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.

Khan spoke to the BBC after visiting refugee camps in eastern Chad, where those who had fled the fighting in Darfur told her of the atrocities they had suffered.

Tens of thousands of people were forced to leave their homes in el-Fasher and the UN said the violence there bore the "hallmarks of genocide".

The RSF has denied widespread allegations that killings in the city were ethnically motivated and follow a pattern of the Arab paramilitaries targeting non-Arab populations.

The group insisted the scale of the atrocities had been exaggerated but acknowledged that some violations...
body.zh: 国际刑事法院（ICC）副首席检察官表示，国际刑事法院（ICC）拥有“具体证据”，将准军事快速支援部队（RSF）领导人与最近在苏丹达尔富尔地区犯下的战争罪行联系起来。 纳扎特·沙米姆·汗 (Nazhat Shameem Khan) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，国际刑事法院在对法希尔和朱奈纳市屠杀平民事件的调查中取得了“突破”。 汗说：“正义可能需要一段时间才能伸张到法庭，但我们会实现这一目标。”他补充说，无国界记者组织领导人也与反人类罪有关。 法希尔的围困和占领标志着无国界医生组织与苏丹军队之间持续战争中最血腥的事件之一。 联合国表示，去年 10 月，无国界部队占领法希尔后，已有 6000 多人被杀，而该准军事组织被指控在朱奈纳实施了类似的屠杀。 该组织一再否认在达尔富尔任何地方进行了大范围的杀戮。 周三发布的联合国实况调查团报告还发现了军队和无国界部队在苏丹冲突中广泛实施暴行的证据。 报告称，无国界医生组织武装分子应对大部分针对平民的系统性袭击负责，特别是在达尔富尔，那里的人们因种族原因而成为攻击目标，这“可能构成战争罪和反人类罪”。 据联合国实况调查团称，无国界医生组织战士及其附属团体去年占领法希尔时也实施了性虐待，包括强奸、轮奸、性奴役和其他形式的虐待。 汗在接受英国广播公司采访时谈到国际刑事法院的调查时表示：“我们现在找到了具体证据，通过将证据与领导模式中的特定人员联系起来，将实地发生的事情联系起来。” 然而，她没有给出何时对那些应对 2023 年 4 月开始的战争暴行负责的人提出指控的时间表。 “但我们可以说，进展是显着的，我们已经取得了突破。” 国际刑事法院总部位于荷兰海牙市，是一个全球法院，有权对种族灭绝罪、反人类罪和战争罪提起诉讼。 汗在访问乍得东部的难民营后接受了英国广播公司的采访，那些逃离达尔富尔战斗的人向她讲述了他们所遭受的暴行。 数万人被迫离开法希尔的家园，联合国称那里的暴力带有“种族灭绝的标志”。 无国界医生组织否认了广泛的指控，即该市的杀戮是出于种族动机，并遵循阿拉伯准军事部队针对非阿拉伯人口的模式。 该组织坚称暴行的规模被夸大了，但承认一些违法行为......

reflection.en: The long-awaited breakthrough in the Darfur war crimes probe offers a glimmer of hope where justice has long seemed paralyzed. This development reminds us that even when accountability is slow, the pursuit of truth and righteousness remains vital. Yahweh calls us to never cease advocating for a world where justice flows, even when it feels perverted.
reflection.zh: 达尔富尔战争罪调查的突破，为长期以来似乎停滞不前的公义带来了希望的曙光。这一进展提醒我们，即使追究责任的进程缓慢，对真理和公义的追求仍然至关重要。雅伟呼召我们永不停止倡导一个公义如江河般涌流的世界，即便有时它似乎被扭曲。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: Is the Strait of Hormuz still Iran's trump card?
title.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡仍是伊朗的王牌吗？

summary.en: Iran's recent actions demonstrate its capacity to disrupt global shipping and energy markets, potentially drawing in neighboring Gulf states. The article examines Iran's actual leverage over Washington and the possible repercussions of its high-risk approach.
summary.zh: 伊朗最近的行动表明，它有能力扰乱全球航运和能源市场，并可能牵连海湾邻国。文章探讨了德黑兰对华盛顿的实际影响力，以及其高风险策略可能带来的反作用。

body.en:
Iran's latest attacks show it can easily disrupt shipping, energy markets and draw in Gulf neighbors. DW asks how much leverage Tehran really has over Washington and if its high-risk strategy could backfire.

The Iran war has reignited after Tehran struck at least three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to US and maritime officials.

The attacks, which targeted a Saudi oil tanker and a Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier, prompted the United States  to revoke the temporary sanctions waiver on Iranian oil exports.

This major concession in the memorandum of understanding (MOU) agreed by the US and Iran last month allowed Tehran to restart oil exports after its tankers were halted by a US Navy blockade.

In further retaliation, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Wednesday it had struck more than 80 targets in Iran, including air defense systems, radars and over 60 small boats used by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to harass shipping .

The US military said it followed up Thursday with a fresh round of strikes on around 90 targets.

CENTCOM said it wanted to "impose heavy costs for targeting and attacking commercial shipping crewed by innocent civilians in an international waterway."

Iran then hit back by launching fresh missile strikes on Gulf nations on Wednesday, with air raid sirens and explosions reported in Bahrain and Kuwait . Further strikes were reported Thursday.

Traffic through the strait, which had restarted after the ceasefire deal, had again grinded to a halt, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing shipping tracking data.

Reacting to the escalation, maritime security firm MARISKS warned Wednesday that the tit-for-tat action "marks a return to direct military confrontation."

Speaking ahead of a NATO summit in Turkey, US President Donald Trump said the MOU with Iran was now "over," adding that "It’s just a waste of time dealing with them [Tehran]."

China and Qatar, meanwhile, called for an immediate de-escalation, while German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius called on Tehran to stop provoking Washington and cease attacks on vessels.

Iran is trying to maintain its control over Hormuz, the narrow waterway that before the war carried a fifth of the world's oil and gas exports from the Gulf to the rest of the world.

Iran effectively closed the strait after US-Israeli airstrikes killed several Iranian officials, including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei , on February 28. Later, Iran struck around a dozen ships caught in the strait, before a fragile ceasefire deal was reached last month.

title.en: Platner's disastrous candidacy exposes rifts that could dampen Democrats' Senate hopes
title.zh: 普拉特纳灾难性的候选资格暴露裂痕，可能削弱民主党在参议院的希望

summary.en: Graham Platner's failed candidacy has not only caused disruption in a crucial Senate race for Democrats but has also exposed deep divisions between the party's progressive and moderate factions.
summary.zh: 格雷厄姆·普拉特纳的失败竞选不仅给民主党一场必胜的参议院竞选带来了混乱，也暴露了该党左翼和温和派之间的深刻分歧。

body.en:
Graham Platner's meteoric rise from relative obscurity to the Democratic nominee in this year's marquee US Senate contest has now ended in catastrophic collapse.

The oysterman and former Marine who beat a popular governor and built a grassroots network of more than 15,000 supporters in Maine announced he was suspending his campaign on Wednesday night .

The news came via recorded video posted on social media , just a little more than 48 hours after Politico published a story containing allegations from an ex-girlfriend that an intoxicated Platner had entered her home uninvited in 2021 and sexually assaulted her. He has denied the allegation.

"We went toe to toe with one of the most entrenched political systems in the history of the world, and we won," Platner said in his 11-minute video announcing the end of his campaign. "And now they are not going to let us have it, not if it's me."

Platner, who had been championed by liberal stalwarts like Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders and Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren, was his party's chosen challenger to unseat five-term Senator Susan Collins – the only Republican in Congress representing a state that Democrats won in the 2024 presidential election.

To take control of the Senate in November's midterm elections, they have to flip four Republican-held seats while defending all of theirs. Maine is widely considered a must-win target.

Now, Platner's exit is threatening to deal a serious blow to their hopes. It is also re-exposing rifts between the party's left wing and moderates that could not only endanger their success this year but in the 2028 presidential race as well.

The sexual assault allegation against Platner was just the latest, most serious, controversy to dog the novice candidate since he entered the race last August.

Earlier reports of offensive social media posts, a chest tattoo with Nazi connotations, sexually explicit text messages sent to women after he was married in 2023, and allegations from former girlfriends of threatening and "toxic" behaviour did not deter 72% of Maine's Democrats from casting their ballots for him in June's primary.

Platner adamantly denied this latest allegation, but within hours of the interview's publication, his political support evaporated. State and national Democrats, including his closest allies on the progressive left - Warren and Sanders included - withdrew their backing. The national party announced it would no longer help finance his campaign. By midweek, it became clear it was only a matter of when, not if, Platner would step aside.

In announcing the end of his campaign, Platner said he was not stepping down because of the allegation.

"We're doing it because of the structures that are being taken away from us by those in power," he added,...
body.zh: 格雷厄姆·普拉特纳(Graham Platner)在今年的美国参议院竞选中从相对默默无闻的人物迅速崛起为民主党候选人，但现在却以灾难性的失败告终。 这位牡蛎手和前海军陆战队员击败了一位受欢迎的州长，并在缅因州建立了一个由 15,000 多名支持者组成的草根网络，他于周三晚上宣布暂停竞选活动。 这一消息是通过社交媒体上发布的录制视频发布的，就在 48 小时多一点后，Politico 发表了一篇报道，其中包含一名前女友的指控，称醉酒的普拉特纳在 2021 年不请自来地进入她家并对她进行了性侵犯。他否认了这一指控。 普拉特纳在宣布竞选结束的 11 分钟视频中表示：“我们与世界历史上最根深蒂固的政治制度之一正面交锋，我们赢了。” “现在他们不会让我们拥有它，如果是我的话也不会。” 普拉特纳受到佛蒙特州参议员伯尼·桑德斯和马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦等自由派坚定支持者的支持，他是该党选定的挑战者，以推翻五届参议员苏珊·柯林斯——国会中唯一代表民主党在 2024 年总统选举中获胜的州的共和党人。 为了在 11 月的中期选举中控制参议院，他们必须推翻共和党控制的四个席位，同时捍卫自己的所有席位。缅因州被广泛认为是必须获胜的目标。 现在，普拉特纳的退出可能会对他们的希望造成严重打击。这也再次暴露了该党左翼和温和派之间的裂痕，这不仅会危及他们今年的成功，还会危及 2028 年总统竞选。 自去年八月参加竞选以来，普拉特纳的性侵犯指控只是困扰这位新手候选人的最新、最严重的争议。 此前有关社交媒体帖子的攻击性报道、带有纳粹含义的胸部纹身、他在 2023 年结婚后向女性发送的露骨色情短信以及前女友的威胁和“有毒”行为的指控，都没有阻止 72% 的缅因州民主党人在 6 月的初选中为他投票。 普拉特纳坚决否认这一最新指控，但在采访发表后几个小时内，他的政治支持就消失了。州和全国民主党人，包括他在进步左派中最亲密的盟友——沃伦和桑德斯——撤回了支持。国家党宣布将不再资助他的竞选活动。到了周中，情况变得很明显，普拉特纳下台只是时间问题，而不是是否会下台的问题。 普拉特纳在宣布竞选结束时表示，他不会因为这一指控而辞职。 他补充说：“我们这样做是因为当权者正在从我们手中夺走结构。”

reflection.en: Political divisions, especially within a party, can undermine collective goals and dampen hopes for shared success. Yahweh's word encourages us to act not from selfish ambition or conceit, but with humility, valuing others above ourselves. This posture can help bridge divides and foster unity, even amidst differing viewpoints.

title.en: Trump may have offered Ukraine exactly what it wants. But there's a major catch

body.en:
One of the "world's best missiles" could be manufactured in Ukraine as part of its defence against Russia, but experts say it's only good news "down the road" for the war-torn nation.

Speaking at a NATO summit overnight, United States President Donald Trump offered to give Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

The missiles are one of the only weapons capable of countering Russia's most brutal attacks, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has been asking for them for years and more recently for a licence to manufacture them.

Russian ballistic missile strikes have killed dozens of Ukrainians in the past week and caused significant damage to infrastructure.

While Trump's offer could be a lifeline to Ukraine, it could be too little and too late in its war with Russia, as the president also considers his relationship with other world leaders.

Patriot missiles are a little over 5m in length, 40cm in diameter, and have a range of 70km, the Associated Press reports.

The missiles are fired from a battery that costs approximately $US10 million ($14.4 million) to manufacture and can require as many as 90 troops to operate and maintain it.

Oleksandra Molloy, a senior lecturer in aviation safety at the University of New South Wales, told SBS News that the Patriots are widely regarded as among the world's most capable air defence missiles.

"They are very effective at downing incoming ballistic missiles, which fly at much higher altitudes and are much faster than other types of missiles or drones," she said.

The US has previously provided these missiles to Ukraine for its defence, but intelligence suggests the country now has limited means to defend against Russian strikes.

Douglas Lute, a former US ambassador to NATO, said it's likely Ukraine has run out of defensive missiles, leaving it vulnerable.

"Recently, none of the incoming Russian ballistic missiles has been downed. That suggests that Ukraine is essentially out of its Patriot air defence system," he told ABC Radio National on Thursday morning.

When asked if the United States would send additional Patriot interceptors immediately, Trump said "some" could be sent immediately and that he thought Ukraine could begin to produce its own quickly.

"We have Patriots, but we don't have that many. We need them for ourselves too," he said.

Lute estimated that it takes the US around two years to produce the defensive missiles, saying that while Ukraine has a strong defence industry, manufacturing Patriots could be a challenge.

title.en: US launches more strikes on Iran with blasts reported in south of country
title.zh: 美国对伊朗发动更多袭击，据报该国南部发生爆炸

summary.en: The United States has launched further strikes against Iran, with reports of blasts in the country's south. President Trump stated these attacks were "retribution for yesterday's bombing of ships by Iran," following Iran's earlier pledge of strong retaliation.
summary.zh: 美国对伊朗发动了更多袭击，据报道该国南部发生爆炸。特朗普总统表示，这些袭击是“对伊朗昨日轰炸船只的报复”，此前伊朗曾誓言将进行强力报复。

body.en:
The US has launched a new round of strikes on Iran after President Donald Trump signalled he would "hit them hard again tonight" following an exchange of attacks on Tuesday.

Explosions have been reported by Iranian state media in parts of the country's south, including Sirik and Bandar Abbas - port cities on the Strait of Hormuz.

After the latest strikes, Trump said in a post on Truth Social: "This is in retribution for yesterday's bombing of ships by Iran. If it happens again, it will get much worse!"

Gulf nations reported Iranian attacks following the US strikes, with explosions in Bahrain's capital Manama, Kuwait intercepting missiles and drones, and Qatar issuing a security alert.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has confirmed that it launched retaliatory strikes on US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain overnight, and called them the "first phase of the punitive response against the American treaty-breakers".

Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who is also the country's chief negotiator with the US, said on X that America "still hasn't learned that bullying and breaking promises are no longer cost-free".

"Let me put it plainly: if you strike, you'll get hit," he wrote, adding that the Strait of Hormuz will only open under Iranian arrangements - not "American threats".

US Central Command (Centcom) said the most recent round of strikes was carried out to "further degrade Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping and innocent civilian mariners" in the vital waterway.

In a statement it said it had struck 90 Iranian military targets, which included air defense systems and military logistics infrastructure along Iran's coastline.

"The latest strikes follow successful execution of offensive strikes in Iran the night before," Centcom added.

Several explosions have also reportedly been heard in other parts of the Iranian coast, including the cities of Konarak and Chabahar.

Iranian state TV reported eight explosions in Bandar Abbas, and said two missiles had hit the ports of both Sirik and Jask - also in southern Iran.

It added that two projectiles had hit the island of Abu Musa, which has been the subject of a longstanding ownership dispute between Iran and the United Arab Emirates.

Air defence systems have been activated in Bandar Abbas, according to reports in Iranian state media.

The extent of damage from the US strikes is not yet known, but Iranian media have reported power cuts in Chabahar and a fire at an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) barracks in Bushehr.

Two of three power lines cut off in Chabahar had been restored quickly and a third would be operational soon, the Iranian Students' News Agency said.

title.en: Albanese and Modi ink uranium deal, as tens of thousands gather for 'significant' visit
title.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯和莫迪签署铀协议，数万人聚集迎接“重要”访问

summary.en: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed a uranium deal, allowing Australia to export uranium to India for "peaceful purposes." The agreement was part of a significant visit by Albanese to India.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯与印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪签署了一项铀协议，允许澳大利亚向印度出口用于“和平目的”的铀。该协议是阿尔巴尼斯对印度进行重要访问的一部分。

body.en:
Australia will export uranium to India under a new agreement signed today between Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as the leader of the world's most populous country continues his visit to Australia.

"Today we can confirm the signing of the administrative arrangement to export uranium to India for peaceful purposes under the 2015 Australia-India nuclear cooperative agreement," Albanese told reporters in Canberra.

The agreement "facilitates Australian uranium exports to India to help increase the share of non-fossil fuel power capacity, providing an additional market for the Australian resources sector".

The 2015 agreement allowed Australian companies to export uranium to India on a commercial basis, but India's possession of nuclear weapons butted against Australia's nuclear safeguards, which meant uranium could only be exported for peaceful purposes.

Calling India a "top-tier" security partner, Albanese announced a raft of pledges he said reflected their shared vision for a peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific, including the development of a Memorandum of Understanding on the provision of defence services, and the repatriation of remains held in cultural institutions both in India and Australia.

Among the new measures, Albanese announced a temporary space-tracking terminal on Cocos Keeling Islands will support India's Human Space Flight program, which aims to send humans into space by 2027.

Australia will also re-award permanent major project status for Project Ceres, a urea manufacturing development in Karratha in Western Australia — producing nitrogen-based fertilizer to address disruptions in the global supply chain by the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz.

Not many world leaders can sell out an arena during an international diplomatic visit.

But tens of thousands of members of the Indian diaspora throughout Australia are expected to make their way to Melbourne's Docklands Stadium on Thursday night for a glimpse of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Modi arrived in Australia on Wednesday for a three-day trip as part of the Australia-India Annual Leaders' Summit, where he will meet with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.

A group of supporters of the Khalistan movement gathered to protest Modi's visit, outside an event at Government House on Thursday.

The Khalistan movement broadly advocates for a separate homeland for Sikhs, and has faced suppression by the Indian government.

During previous visits, Modi made public appearances in Sydney , drawing crowds of thousands of people.

body.zh: 随着世界上人口最多国家的领导人继续访问澳大利亚，澳大利亚将根据安东尼·阿尔巴内斯总理和印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪今天签署的新协议向印度出口铀。 阿尔巴内斯在堪培拉对记者表示：“今天我们可以确认签署了根据2015年澳大利亚-印度核合作协议向印度出口用于和平目的的铀的行政安排。” 该协议“促进澳大利亚向印度出口铀，以帮助增加非化石燃料发电能力的份额，为澳大利亚资源行业提供额外的市场”。 2015年的协议允许澳大利亚公司在商业基础上向印度出口铀，但印度拥有核武器与澳大利亚的核保障措施相抵触，这意味着铀只能用于和平目的出口。 阿尔巴尼斯称印度为“顶级”安全伙伴，并宣布了一系列承诺，他说这反映了他们对和平与繁荣的印太地区的共同愿景，包括制定一份关于提供国防服务的谅解备忘录，以及归还印度和澳大利亚文化机构中的遗骸。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 在新措施中，阿尔巴尼斯宣布科科斯基林群岛上的一个临时太空跟踪终端将支持印度的载人太空飞行计划，该计划旨在于 2027 年将人类送入太空。 澳大利亚还将重新授予 Ceres 项目永久重大项目地位，Ceres 项目是西澳大利亚卡拉萨的尿素制造开发项目，生产氮肥，以解决霍尔木兹海峡封锁造成的全球供应链中断问题。 没有多少世界领导人能够在国际外交访问期间出售一个场地。 但预计周四晚上，澳大利亚各地数万名印度侨民将前往墨尔本港区体育场，一睹印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪的风采。 莫迪于周三抵达澳大利亚，开始为期三天的访问，作为澳大利亚-印度年度领导人峰会的一部分，他将在峰会上会见总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞。 周四，一群哈利斯坦运动的支持者聚集在政府大楼外抗议莫迪的访问。 卡利斯坦运动广泛主张为锡克教徒建立一个独立的家园，并面临印度政府的打压。 在之前的访问中，莫迪在悉尼公开露面，吸引了数千人围观。 这次，他将在阿尔巴尼斯的陪同下，在一场已预订满的活动上发表讲话。

title.en: Democrat Graham Platner suspends campaign for key US Senate race after assault allegation
title.zh: 民主党人格雷厄姆·普拉特纳因性侵指控暂停参议院竞选

summary.en: Democrat Graham Platner has suspended his campaign for a key US Senate race. This decision follows a woman's accusation of sexual assault, which Platner has publicly stated is "categorically false."
summary.zh: 民主党人格雷厄姆·普拉特纳已暂停其在美国参议院关键席位的竞选活动。此前，一名女性指控他性侵，普拉特纳对此坚称“完全不实”。

body.en:
Democrat Graham Platner has suspended his campaign for US Senate in Maine, following a series of scandals that included a woman accusing him of sexual assault.

In the days since the accusation was made, Democrats have called on him to drop out of the race considered pivotal to their chances of gaining control of the US Senate.

In a video posted online, Platner said his decision was not an admission of guilt but due to Democrats' threats to cut off campaign support. He called the assault allegation "false".

He said he would officially file to withdraw from the race once he's assured his replacement in the race against Republican Susan Collins is selected in a "transparent and democratic" way.

"We're suspending campaign operations," he said in an 11-minute video posted to X, adding that he would file his paperwork to withdraw only after he was assured the process to replace him would be "open and democratic moving forward".

Platner added that he is not "trying to dictate to anyone who it should be or how we get there".

"But I will say this: it needs to be open, transparent, and democratic. It needs to be reflecting the will and the values of the people that built this movement," he said.

Under state law, Platner has to officially drop out by 13 July for a replacement name to be put on the ballot.

The race is one of several pivotal to Democrats eyeing a longshot bid to flip control of the Senate in November's congressional elections, commonly called the midterms.

Maine is considered a must-win state for Democrats to take the majority in the Senate. But it's an uphill battle. The party must flip Collins' seat, hold on to all their existing seats and gain three more in the November midterm election.

Platner, an oyster farmer and military veteran, rocketed to the top of the Democratic field with a message of plain-spoken populism.

He championed progressive policies like universal health care and affordable housing, and won over many frustrated Democratic voters with his critique of the party's establishment.

Endorsements from two liberal leaders, Senators Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren, bolstered his candidacy. His momentum was so strong that his opponent for the nomination, Maine Governor Janet Mills, suspended her campaign.

The assault allegation was made public on Monday. By that night, Warren and other top Democrats called for him to withdraw and three of his strongest supporters in Congress - Representatives Ro Khanna and Senators Ruben Gallego and Martin Heinrich - had rescinded their endorsements.

The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which provides millions of dollars in support to the party's candidates, and the Maine Democratic party had both ended their backing, too.

body.zh: 民主党人格雷厄姆·普拉特纳（Graham Platner）在发生一系列丑闻（其中包括一名妇女指控他性侵犯）后，暂停了缅因州美国​​参议院的竞选活动。 在提出指控后的几天里，民主党人呼吁他退出竞选，这被认为对他们获得美国参议院控制权的机会至关重要。 在网上发布的视频中，普拉特纳表示，他的决定并不是认罪，而是由于民主党威胁要切断竞选支持。他称袭击指控是“错误的”。 他表示，一旦他确保以“透明和民主”的方式选出与共和党人苏珊·柯林斯竞争的替代者，他将正式申请退出竞选。 他在发布到 X 的一段 11 分钟视频中表示，“我们将暂停竞选活动”，并补充说，只有在他确信接替他的程序将“公开、民主地推进”后，他才会提交退出文件。 普拉特纳补充说，他并不是“试图向任何人指示应该是谁或者我们如何到达那里”。 “但我要说的是：它需要公开、透明和民主。它需要反映发起这场运动的人们的意愿和价值观，”他说。 根据州法律，普拉特纳必须在 7 月 13 日之前正式退出，以便将替代名字列入选票。 对于民主党人来说，这场竞选是关键的几项关键竞选之一，他们希望在 11 月的国会选举（通常称为中期选举）中夺取参议院控制权，但希望渺茫。 缅因州被认为是民主党必须赢得参议院多数席位的州。但这是一场艰苦的战斗。该党必须推翻柯林斯的席位，保住所有现有席位，并在 11 月中期选举中再获得三个席位。 普拉特纳是一位牡蛎养殖者和退伍军人，他凭借直言不讳的民粹主义信息一跃成为民主党领域的顶峰。 他倡导全民医疗保健和经济适用住房等进步政策，并通过对民主党建制派的批评赢得了许多沮丧的民主党选民的支持。 参议员伯尼·桑德斯和伊丽莎白·沃伦两位自由派领导人的支持支持了他的候选资格。他的势头如此强劲，以至于他的提名对手、缅因州州长珍妮特·米尔斯暂停了她的竞选活动。 袭击指控于周一公开。那天晚上，沃伦和其他民主党高层呼吁他退出，他在国会的三位最强有力的支持者——众议员罗·卡纳、参议员鲁本·加列戈和马丁·海因里希——也撤销了他们的支持。 为该党候选人提供数百万美元支持的民主党参议员竞选委员会和缅因州民主党也都结束了对他们的支持。 虽然普拉特纳的非政治背景有所提升……

reflection.en: In public life, accusations and denials often create complex situations where discerning the full truth is challenging. Proverbs 18:17 reminds us that while the first account may seem convincing, true wisdom requires hearing all sides and careful examination. This situation calls for patience and a commitment to justice, allowing due process to unfold...
reflection.zh: 在公共生活中，指控与否认常常造成复杂局面，要辨明真相充满挑战。箴言18:17提醒我们，虽然先陈述案情的人似乎有理，但真正的智慧需要倾听各方并仔细查验。这种情况呼唤着耐心和对公义的承诺，让正当程序得以进行，而不是急于下判断。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Watch: We're a step closer to finding out if bees have feelings, here's why
title.zh: 观看：我们离发现蜜蜂是否有感情又近了一步，原因在此

summary.en: New research indicates that bumblebees exhibit "emotion-like behaviours," a phenomenon previously observed only in mammals. This discovery brings scientists closer to understanding whether these insects experience feelings.
summary.zh: 新研究发现，大黄蜂表现出“类似情绪的行为”，这种现象此前仅在哺乳动物身上观察到。这一发现使科学家们离了解这些昆虫是否拥有情感更近了一步。

body.en:
In a first-of-its-kind study from Australia's Macquarie University, in collaboration with Southern Medical University in China, researchers observed bees showing "emotion-like behaviours" previously only seen in mammals.

The BBC's Australia reporter Lana Lam explains how their work suggests that bees might have a much richer inner life than ever thought before.
body.zh: 在澳大利亚麦考瑞大学与中国南方医科大学合作进行的一项首次研究中，研究人员观察到蜜蜂表现出以前只在哺乳动物中出现的“类似情绪的行为”。 BBC 澳大利亚记者拉娜·林 (Lana Lam) 解释了他们的研究如何表明蜜蜂的内心生活可能比以前想象的要丰富得多。

reflection.en: This fascinating research reminds us that creation holds deep wisdom, often revealed when we carefully observe the world around us. Yahweh's intricate design is evident even in the smallest creatures, inviting us to learn from their complex lives. Such discoveries can deepen our appreciation for the vastness and wonder of all life.
reflection.zh: 这项引人入胜的研究提醒我们，受造界蕴含着深刻的智慧，当我们仔细观察周围的世界时，这些智慧常被揭示出来。雅伟精妙的设计在最小的生物身上也显而易见，邀请我们从它们复杂的生命中学习。这样的发现能加深我们对所有生命的浩瀚与奇妙的欣赏。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: This hard-right politician quit parliament for a fight. His only rival dresses as a bin
title.zh: 这位强硬右翼政客为一场斗争辞去议员职务。他唯一的对手打扮成一个垃圾桶

summary.en: A man wearing a bin on his head could be the sole challenger for an infamous far-right British politician in a snap by-election.
summary.zh: 一名头戴垃圾桶的男子可能成为英国一位臭名昭著的极右翼政客在一次紧急补选中唯一的挑战者。

body.en:
British anti-immigrant politician Nigel Farage faces the embarrassing prospect of going head-to-head with perennial joke candidate Count Binface in a by-election after he decided to quit parliament.

Comedian Jonathan David Harvey, better known as Count Binface, has stood in multiple elections in the United Kingdom wearing his trademark bin-shaped helmet.

Farage's surprise move now threatens to backfire after other heavyweight parties confirmed they would not contest the vote for Farage's seat in southeast England.

Count Binface, a self-described "intergalactic space warrior", is the only other person to have said so far that they would run.

In a televised address on Tuesday, the leader of the hard-right Reform UK party said he was resigning as the member of parliament for Clacton, the constituency he has represented since July 2024.

The shock announcement came as Farage is the subject of a parliamentary probe over the non-disclosure of a £5 million ($9.65 million) donation from Thailand-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.

The donation was made shortly before Farage was elected an MP and was revealed earlier this year by The Guardian newspaper, which reported earlier this week that bankers raised concern with the National Crime Agency that it may have been laundered money.

The agency told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency it would not confirm whether a complaint had been made.

Farage, whose party leads national opinion polls, also faces scrutiny over separate alleged gifts from George Cottrell, a 32-year-old crypto entrepreneur previously convicted of fraud.

Farage insists he has done nothing wrong and accused opponents in parliament of using sleaze investigations as a "political tool" against him.

The Reform UK leader did, however, discuss cryptocurrencies with Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey in September 2025.

In a letter to a Labour MP seen by AFP, Bailey said the bank was regularly subjected to lobbying and "no policy changes have taken place as a result of interventions by Mr Farage".

In showmanship typical of the 62-year-old Brexit campaigner, Farage said he would seek re-election, pitching the vote as a "people versus the establishment by-election" fight.

title.en: Trump trashes NATO at latest gathering before a message of 'love'
title.zh: 特朗普在最新会议上抨击北约，随后又传递“爱”的信息

summary.en: The US president's remarks at a recent NATO gathering fluctuated significantly, moving from expressions of strong disapproval to declarations of success within a few hours, amidst reports of increased defense spending by European nations.

body.en:
US President Donald Trump offered NATO allies an unexpected warm embrace as they wrapped up a key summit after earlier lashing out over their response to his war on Iran.

It was an abrupt swing from antagonism to affection within the space of a few short hours, illustrating the wide range of emotions exhibited by the mercurial US leader.

"It was amazing, actually. The unity in that room was incredible, really a love, it was sort of pretty wild," Trump told reporters after the closed-door meeting of 32 leaders at the NATO summit in the Turkish capital Ankara

Behind closed doors, Trump had reassured his counterparts he wanted the US to stay in the military alliance, saying: "We want to remain with you", a source inside the session told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

European leaders showcased their surging defence spending at the summit as they looked to convince Trump they're making good on a pledge to ramp up budgets — and take more responsibility for their own security.

"I’m returning to Germany with the sense that we have made a major contribution: that NATO is holding together, that it is becoming stronger, and that it is becoming more European," said German Chancellor Frederich Merz.

But the day had not begun well with Trump lashing out over NATO allies' failure to back his Iran campaign just before the session, threatening to cut trade with Spain, and insisting he still wants NATO member Denmark's territory of Greenland.

"I'm very upset with NATO... because of what they did with Greenland, and... because of the fact that they didn't want to help us with the number one state sponsor of terror, that's Iran," he said.

Once Trump came face-to-face with the leaders behind closed doors, his tone changed markedly, according to the source who attended the talks.

"There is a strong contrast between what Trump says in public and what he actually says inside," he told AFP.

Afterwards, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez insisted that ties with Washington were "very positive".

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said that Trump moderated his tone in the session, telling AFP he had given a "kind of constructive message... that Europe must step up, invest more in defence".

title.en: Trump's support for Venezuela opposition head Machado wanes
title.zh: 特朗普对委内瑞拉反对派领导人马查多的支持减弱

summary.en: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace laureate María Corina Machado says she wants to return to her earthquake-ravaged homeland. Yet neither Venezuela's government nor the United States thinks that's a good idea.
summary.zh: 委内瑞拉反对派领导人、诺贝尔和平奖得主玛丽亚·科里纳·马查多表示，她希望返回遭受地震破坏的祖国。然而，委内瑞拉政府和美国都认为这不是一个好主意。

body.en:
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace laureate María Corina Machado says she wants to return to her earthquake-ravaged homeland. Yet neither Venezuela's government nor the United States thinks that's a good idea.

The opposition politician Maria Corina Machado has been planning her return from the United States to Venezuela for months. When the devastating double earthquake  hit the coastal region of La Guaira in June, she believed that the time was right. In a video message, the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize winner  accused  Venezuela's interim government, led by Delcy Rodríguez , of actively obstructing disaster relief. This accusation is also voiced by earthquake victims and some aid organizations.

Machado recorded the video in Panama City . From there, she planned to fly to Venezuela. Sources close to her allege that Venezuela's government threatened the airline with a landing ban if Machado were on board. Neither Copa Airlines nor Venezuela's government has confirmed the claim, nor have they denied it.

In the video, Machado does not mention an incident that The Wall Street Journal reported in early July. According to the article , in June Machado attempted to fly from the United States to the Dutch-held Caribbean island of Curacao by private jet and then to travel to Venezuela by boat. In December, she had secretly traveled the same route in the opposite direction to fly to Oslo for the Nobel Prize ceremony.

Citing high-level sources, The Wall Street Journal reports that the private jet provided for Machado was over the state of North Carolina when it was ordered back by the US government. The State Department justified demanding that the plane turn back over concerns that political disputes could further complicate relief efforts following the earthquakes.

The conservative Machado was long considered the most important ally within the Venezuelan opposition for US President Donald Trump . A New York Times headline on the rift between Machado and the Trump administration  said: "US Undercuts Venezuela's Opposition Leader as She Tries to Return."

Phil Gunson, of the International Crisis Group in Venezuela , told DW that it is clear that the US government does not view Machado as a transitional politician. And he sees at least one good reason for this: "She was really essential to the opposition victory in 2024. But she's not a negotiator. She has a lot of problems even reaching agreements with people on her own side."

Venezuela's electoral commission declared the incumbent president,  Nicolas Maduro , the winner of the 2024 vote, though the result was protested within the country and abroad. International observers said opposition candidate Edmundo Gonzalez had clearly won the election....

title.en: Hungary public media reform begins with black screen apology
title.zh: 匈牙利公共媒体改革以黑屏道歉开始

summary.en: Public service media in Hungary began a reform with a black screen and an apology, as Peter Magyar started to dismantle what was considered a significant tool of power for Viktor Orban.
summary.zh: 匈牙利公共媒体改革启动，以黑屏和道歉开场，彼得·马扎尔开始拆除维克多·欧尔班最强大的权力工具之一。

body.en:
People tuning in to public service media in Hungary on Tuesday were greeted by a black screen and an apology. Peter Magyar has begun dismantling one of Viktor Orban's most potent tools of power.

The disinformation that public service media in Hungary broadcast during the 16 years of Viktor Orban 's rule was one of a kind in the EU .

No other public service media in the EU published lies, hate and propaganda on this scale in recent decades.

Some content was reminiscent of the fascist, antisemitic propaganda of the period between the two world wars; other content was similar to the output of Russian state media.

To give but a few examples: Criminal Arab and African migrants who rape defenseless Hungarian girls; a US billionaire with Jewish Hungarian roots who is destroying Hungary's Christian identity ; the EU's indoctrination of children with " LGBTQ propaganda ;" a Ukrainian mafia state that wants to sacrifice Hungary's younger generation in the war and rob millions of Hungarian pensioners.

At 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the news channel M1 broadcast a black screen with the following message: "Public media should not lie. We are sorry for doing it for so long. Public media will now be reformed so they will be independent and trustworthy. Our news service is currently suspended. Stay tuned!"

All news bulletins and political programs broadcast by Hungary's public television and radio channels were replaced by the same apology/announcement.

Only the website of the news agency MTI, which is also part of the public media holding MTVA, went on posting political news.

Nothing like this has ever happened before at the country's state broadcaster — not even when the Communist dictatorship collapsed in 1989/90 and Hungary began transitioning to democracy.

"A historic day. Today marks the end of propaganda broadcasts on public media platforms," Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar posted on Facebook on Tuesday. "They lied at night, they lied during the day, they lied on every wavelength. That is now over," he wrote.

But there is more to this change than just a black screen and a written apology.

The most senior figures at M1 have been removed from their posts. One of these is M1's director, Zsolt Nemeth (nicknamed "Pitbull" for his highly aggressive, confrontational style), and most of M1's directors of programming and senior news editors.

Just under four hours after the black screen appeared, M1 began broadcasting again at exactly 7:56 p.m.

The choice of time (19:56 CET) was no coincidence. It was a nod to the anti-Communist, anti-Soviet revolution of 1956 that was brutally crushed by Soviet troops.

The choice of film that followed was also highly symbolic: "The Witness" is a 1979 Hungarian classic, a political satire about the horrors of Stalinism...
body.zh: 周二，人们在匈牙利收看公共服务媒体时，看到的是黑屏和道歉。彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar）已开始拆除维克托·欧尔班（Viktor Orban）最有力的权力工具之一。 匈牙利公共服务媒体在欧尔班·维克多 (Viktor Orban) 统治的 16 年期间传播的虚假信息在欧盟是独一无二的。 近几十年来，欧盟没有其他公共服务媒体发表过如此规模的谎言、仇恨和宣传。 有些内容让人想起两次世界大战期间的法西斯主义、反犹太主义宣传；其他内容与俄罗斯官方媒体的输出类似。 仅举几个例子：阿拉伯和非洲移民犯罪，强奸手无寸铁的匈牙利女孩；一位具有犹太匈牙利血统的美国亿万富翁正在摧毁匈牙利的基督教身份；欧盟向儿童灌输“LGBTQ 宣传”；乌克兰黑手党国家想要在战争中牺牲匈牙利的年轻一代并掠夺数百万匈牙利养老金领取者。 下午 4 点周二，新闻频道M1播放黑屏，并显示以下信息：“公共媒体不应该撒谎。我们很抱歉这么长时间了。公共媒体现在将进行改革，使其独立且值得信赖。我们的新闻服务目前已暂停。敬请关注！” 匈牙利公共电视和广播频道播放的所有新闻公报和政治节目都被同样的道歉/公告所取代。 只有通讯社 MTI（也是 MTVA 旗下公共媒体的一部分）的网站继续发布政治新闻。 该国的国家广播公司以前从未发生过这样的事情——即使在 1989/90 年共产主义独裁政权垮台、匈牙利开始向民主过渡时也没有发生过。 “历史性的一天。今天标志着公共媒体平台上宣传广播的结束，”匈牙利总理彼得·马扎尔周二在脸书上发帖称。 “他们在晚上撒谎，他们在白天撒谎，他们在每个波长上撒谎。现在一切都结束了，”他写道。 但这一变化不仅仅是黑屏和书面道歉。 M1 的最高层人物已被免职。其中之一是 M1 的总监 Zsolt Nemeth（因其高度攻击性、对抗性的风格而被昵称为“斗牛犬”），以及 M1 的大多数节目总监和高级新闻编辑。 黑屏出现后不到四个小时，M1 于晚上 7 点 56 分整再次开始广播。 时间的选择（欧洲中部时间 19:56）并非巧合。这是对 1956 年被苏联军队残酷镇压的反共、反苏革命的致敬。 接下来的电影选择也极具象征意义：《证人》是一部 1979 年的匈牙利经典电影，一部关于斯大林主义恐怖的政治讽刺作品……

reflection.en: The public apology and reform of state media in Hungary highlight the importance of truthfulness in public discourse. When institutions that shape public understanding are reformed, it reflects a desire to put away falsehood and speak truth, fostering trust and integrity. Yahweh calls us to speak truth with our neighbors, a principle vital for healthy...
reflection.zh: 匈牙利公共媒体的公开道歉和改革，凸显了公共言论中诚实的重要性。当塑造公众理解的机构进行改革时，这反映出一种摒弃谎言、讲求真理的愿望，从而培养信任和正直。雅伟呼召我们对邻舍说实话，这是健康社会至关重要的原则。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: US birthright citizenship ruling eases fears among Indians
title.zh: 美国出生公民权裁决缓解了印度裔群体的担忧

summary.en: A recent US Supreme Court decision on birthright citizenship has alleviated anxieties and brought greater stability for Indian families residing in the United States.
summary.zh: 美国最高法院近期关于出生公民权的裁决，缓解了居住在美国的印度裔家庭的担忧，并减少了不确定性。

body.en:
The recent US Supreme Court ruling on birthright citizenship has eased concerns and reduced uncertainty for Indian families living in the United States.

The US Supreme Court's recent decision to leave birthright citizenship intact offers relief to thousands of Indian families, even as the political battle over who deserves to be American is far from over.  

When the top court's ruling came through on June 30, Rajesh and Neha, an Indian couple living in Seattle, read the news over breakfast before leaving for work.

Rajesh, a software engineer, moved to the US from the southern Indian city of Bengaluru in 2016 on an H-1B visa . Neha joined him a year later. Their six-year-old daughter, Aanya, was born in the United States.

"It was a relief," Neha told DW. "For months, we kept wondering if something so fundamental could really change."

Their daughter remains an American citizen. But for her parents, little else has changed. Like thousands of Indian professionals in the US, they are still waiting for employment-based green cards after years in the queue.

"We're happy our daughter's future is protected," said Rajesh. "But we're still living one visa renewal at a time."

The US Supreme Court at the end of June left birthright citizenship intact, ruling that children born on US soil remain citizens regardless of their parents' immigration status.

US President Donald Trump signed an executive order last year decreeing that children born to parents in the United States illegally or on temporary visas would not automatically become US citizens.

"The ruling is a profound affirmation of who belongs in America," said Chintan Patel, executive director of Indian American Impact, a civic and political advocacy organization.

"Indian and South Asian immigrant families are among those most directly threatened by Trump's executive order, communities navigating long visa backlogs and uncertain immigration timelines, where children are often born here long before their parents have a clear path to permanence," said Patel in a statement.

Indians are the second-largest Asian-origin group in the US after Chinese Americans, according to a May 2025 Pew Research Center fact sheet.

About 5.2 million people of Indian origin lived in the US in 2023, roughly 21% of the country's population of Asian origin.

Indians are the largest recipients of H-1B visas, the program that lets US companies hire skilled foreign workers. They also face the longest waits for employment-based green cards, because of per country caps.

Community organizations estimate that hundreds of thousands of children have been born in the US to Indian parents on temporary work visas.

body.zh: 美国最高法院最近对出生公民权的裁决缓解了居住在美国的印度家庭的担忧并减少了不确定性。 美国最高法院最近决定保留与生俱来的公民身份，这让成千上万的印度家庭松了一口气，尽管关于谁应该成为美国人的政治斗争还远未结束。 6 月 30 日最高法院作出裁决后，居住在西雅图的一对印度夫妇拉杰什 (Rajesh) 和尼哈 (Neha) 在上班前吃早餐时读到了这条新闻。 Rajesh 是一名软件工程师，2016 年持 H-1B 签证从印度南部城市班加罗尔移居美国。一年后，尼哈加入了他。他们六岁的女儿安雅出生在美国。 “这让人松了一口气，”内哈告诉德国之声。 “几个月来，我们一直想知道如此根本的事情是否真的可以改变。” 他们的女儿仍然是美国公民。但对于她的父母来说，其他方面没有什么改变。与成千上万在美国的印度专业人士一样，他们在排队多年后仍在等待就业绿卡。 “我们很高兴我们女儿的未来得到了保护，”拉杰什说。 “但我们仍然处于一次续签签证的状态。” 六月底，美国最高法院维持与生俱来的公民身份不变，裁定在美国领土上出生的儿童仍然是公民，无论其父母的移民身份如何。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普去年签署了一项行政命令，规定父母在美国非法或持有临时签证所生的孩子不会自动成为美国公民。 “这项裁决是对谁属于美国的深刻肯定，”公民和政治倡导组织印度裔美国影响力组织的执行董事金坦·帕特尔说。 帕特尔在一份声明中表示：“印度和南亚移民家庭是受到特朗普行政命令最直接威胁的人群之一，社区面临长期签证积压和不确定的移民时间表，孩子们往往早在父母找到明确的永久居留权之前就出生在这里。” 根据皮尤研究中心 2025 年 5 月的情况说明书，印度人是美国第二大亚裔群体，仅次于华裔美国人。 2023 年，约有 520 万印度裔人口居住在美国，约占该国亚裔人口的 21%。 印度人是 H-1B 签证的最大接受者，该计划允许美国公司雇用熟练的外国工人。由于每个国家的上限，他们还面临着以就业为基础的绿卡的最长等待时间。 社区组织估计，持有临时工作签证的印度父母在美国生下了数十万儿童。 法院的裁决现在保留了他们的公民身份以及随之而来的权利，包括美国......

reflection.en: The Supreme Court's ruling brings relief to families who have made the U.S. their home, affirming a sense of belonging and reducing uncertainty. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to treat those residing among us as native-born, recognizing their dignity and right to security. This principle fosters a society where all can thrive, free from the anxiety of...
reflection.zh: 最高法院的裁决为那些已在美国安家的家庭带来了宽慰，确认了他们的归属感并减少了不确定性。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，要善待居住在我们中间的外国人，视他们如同本地人，承认他们的尊严和获得安全的权利。这一原则有助于建立一个所有人都能够繁荣发展的社会，免受不确定身份的困扰。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

In such times, we are called to care for both human safety and the wider...

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.

title.en: 'The water just came so fast': Typhoon triggers floods and rare tornadoes in China
title.zh: “水来得太快了”：台风在中国引发洪水和罕见龙卷风

summary.en: Villagers whose families have been stranded told the BBC they are struggling to get food and help after a typhoon triggered floods and rare tornadoes in China.
summary.zh: 台风在中国引发洪水和罕见龙卷风后，受困村民告诉英国广播公司，他们的家人被困，正在努力获取食物和帮助。

body.en:
On Sunday, heavy rain began falling on Renhe village in the southern Chinese province of Guangxi.

The villagers were used to it. But the rain didn't stop - and the water suddenly rose.

By the early hours of Monday, the water had reached their knees. By dawn, it had completely submerged the first floor of their homes.

"The floods happened so rapidly, the water just came so fast. The villagers didn't have time to take food with them when they were running away," a woman from Renhe, whose surname is Zhou, told the BBC.

Zhou's family is among tens of thousands of people in Guangxi displaced from their homes since Typhoon Maysak swept the region over the weekend, causing rivers to swell and dam walls to break. At least four people have died.

The typhoon has inundated the city of Nanning and surrounding villages, with residents calling for rescue from their rooftops.

It has also triggered thunderstorms, and even tornadoes, in the central province of Hubei - hundreds of kilometres away.

At least 17 people have died, hundreds more have been injured and tens of thousands have been evacuated, according to state media.

The devastation from days of extreme weather has prompted President Xi Jinping to order "all out" rescue and relief operations.

Typhoons that cause widespread flooding are common in China at this time of the year and Maysak is the first to make landfall in the country for the 2026 season.

State media said it has been characterised by "its sudden onset and intense, short-duration winds".

Another storm, Super Typhoon Bavi, is churning across the Pacific, on course to hit China's eastern coast later this week, according to forecasts.

Authorities in Nanning have warned that "extremely heavy rain" could hamper rescue efforts.

Extreme weather, which experts link to climate change, have increasingly threatened China's residents and economy - especially its trillion-dollar agriculture sector.

Residents from Guangxi province have told the BBC that thousands remain trapped on rooftops, some in mountain villages, because of the floods.

The official count estimates 60,000 people have been evacuated and at least 90,000 in total are affected by the deluge.

Zhou, who is currently living in another province, said some of her family members are still trapped in their homes in Renhe and have limited food. Her four-month-old niece has gone for more than a day without milk.

"Other villagers are gathering at higher ground, but they are running out of supplies as well. There are too many villages affected, and not enough rescue workers."

Another woman, whose surname is Huang, from the town of Yunbiao said it took just 10 minutes for floods to submerge villages in her area.

"We simply couldn't rescue everyone in time. There were too few rescue...
body.zh: 周日，中国南部广西省人和村开始下大雨。 村民们已经习惯了。但雨并没有停——水位突然上涨。 到周一凌晨，水位已经达到了膝盖。到黎明时分，洪水已经完全淹没了他们家的一楼。 “洪水来得如此之快，水来得如此之快。村民们在逃跑时没有时间携带食物，”仁和一位周姓女士告诉BBC。 周末台风美莎克横扫广西，导致河流水位上涨、水坝溃决，周的家人是广西数万名流离失所者中的一员。至少有四人死亡。 台风已经淹没了南宁市和周边村庄，居民在屋顶上呼吁救援。 它还在数百公里外的中部省份湖北引发了雷暴，甚至龙卷风。 据官方媒体报道，至少 17 人死亡，数百人受伤，数万人被疏散。 连日来的极端天气造成的破坏促使习近平主席下令“全力以赴”开展救援行动。 每年这个时候，造成大范围洪水的台风在中国很常见，而“美莎克”是 2026 年第一个在中国登陆的台风。 官方媒体称，此次飓风的特点是“突然来袭、强风、持续时间短”。 据预测，另一场风暴超级台风巴威正在太平洋上肆虐，本周晚些时候将袭击中国东部沿海。 南宁当局警告称，“特大暴雨”可能会阻碍救援工作。 专家将极端天气与气候变化联系起来，它日益威胁着中国的居民和经济，尤其是价值数万亿美元的农业部门。 广西省的居民告诉英国广播公司，由于洪水，数千人仍被困在屋顶上，其中一些人被困在山村里。 官方统计估计已有 60,000 人被疏散，总共至少有 90,000 人受到洪水影响。 目前居住在另一个省份的周说，她的一些家人仍然被困在仁和的家中，食物有限。她四个月大的侄女已经一天多没有喝奶了。 “其他村民正在地势较高的地方聚集，但他们的物资也即将耗尽。受影响的村庄太多，救援人员却不够。” 另一名来自云标镇的黄姓妇女表示，洪水只用了10分钟就淹没了她所在地区的村庄。 “我们根本无法及时营救所有人。营救的人太少了......

reflection.en: The plight of villagers struggling for food and help after a typhoon reminds us of the profound human need for practical compassion in times of crisis. Yahweh's call in Isaiah 58:7 urges us to share our resources with the hungry and provide shelter for the displaced. In such moments, our care for those most vulnerable reflects a deeper commitment to justice...
reflection.zh: 台风过后，村民们为食物和援助而挣扎的困境，提醒我们在危机时刻，人类对实际关怀的深切需求。雅伟在以赛亚书58:7中的呼召，敦促我们与饥饿者分享食物，为流离失所者提供住所。在这样的时刻，我们对最脆弱者的关怀反映了对公义和怜悯的更深承诺。

verse.textEn: Is it not to share your food with the hungry and to provide the poor wanderer with shelter — when you see the naked, to clothe them?
verse.textZh: 不是要把你的饼分给饥饿的人，将飘流的穷人接到你家中，见赤身的给他衣服遮体？

title.en: Plenty of players but no grassroots: can China ever grow into a footballing giant?
title.zh: 球员众多但缺乏基层：中国能否成长为足球巨头？

summary.en: Experts note that despite large crowds at amateur matches, China lacks a robust grassroots system to develop players into professionals, hindering its ambition to become a footballing giant.
summary.zh: 专家指出，尽管中国业余足球比赛吸引了大量观众，但缺乏健全的基层体系将球员培养成职业选手，这阻碍了其成为足球强国的雄心。

body.en: Some of its amateur matches pull in bigger crowds than European leagues but are more of a spectacle than a pathway to the professional game, say experts Michael Owen, a man who once quipped he had never drunk tea or coffee, isn’t known for his adventurous palate. Safe to assume, then, that the former England striker was out of his comfort zone sipping Roxburgh rose juice and eating chilli-wrapped rice noodle rolls during his recent visit to south-west China’s Guizhou province. The 2001 Ballon d’Or winner dusted off his boots for a match in Rongjiang county, the birthplace of viral amateur football league Cun Chao, also known as the Village Super League. Scoring twice in a 4-3 loss for local side Rongjiang Niubi, Owen endeared himself to the thousands in attendance, even if some weren’t familiar with the former Liverpool and Real Madrid player. Continue reading...
body.zh: 专家迈克尔·欧文(Michael Owen)表示，它的一些业余比赛比欧洲联赛吸引了更多的观众，但更多的是一场奇观，而不是进入职业比赛的途径。迈克尔·欧文曾打趣说自己从未喝过茶或咖啡，但他并不以冒险的味觉而闻名。那么，可以肯定的是，这位前英格兰前锋在最近访问中国西南部的贵州省期间，已经走出了自己的舒适区，喝着罗克斯堡玫瑰汁，吃着辣椒卷。这位2001年金球奖得主在榕江县的一场比赛中掸掉了靴子上的灰尘，那里是风靡一时的业余足球联赛存超（也称为乡村超级联赛）的发源地。在当地球队榕江牛鼻子队以4-3输球的比赛中，欧文梅开二度，赢得了数千名现场观众的喜爱，尽管有些人对这位前利物浦和皇家马德里球员并不熟悉。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The challenge of building a strong football culture from the ground up highlights the importance of foundational development. Just as a child needs careful guidance and training to flourish, so too does any endeavor require intentional investment in its earliest stages to achieve lasting success. This reminds us that true growth often begins with nurturing...
reflection.zh: 从基层建立强大足球文化的挑战，突显了基础发展的重要性。正如孩子需要细心引导和培养才能茁壮成长，任何事业也需要对其早期阶段进行有意识的投入，才能取得持久的成功。这提醒我们，真正的成长往往始于在基层培养潜力。

verse.textEn: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
verse.textZh: 教养孩童，使他走当行的道，就是到老他也不偏离。

title.en: Lethal tornado tears through Chinese province amid devastating storms – video
title.zh: 致命龙卷风席卷中国省份，破坏性风暴肆虐——视频

summary.en: Devastating storms, including a lethal tornado, have swept through China's Hubei province, resulting in at least 15 fatalities and the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of residents. Chinese leader Xi Jinping has called for comprehensive rescue efforts for those affected.
summary.zh: 毁灭性风暴，包括一场致命的龙卷风，席卷了中国湖北省，造成至少15人死亡，数十万人被疏散。中国领导人习近平已敦促“全力以赴”救援受灾民众。

body.en: Storms tore through China's Hubei province, killing at least 15 people, according to state media. Hundreds of thousands of people have also been evacuated as devastating storms hit the country. Chinese leader Xi Jinping has urged 'all out' efforts to rescue those affected
body.zh: 据官方媒体报道，暴风雨席卷了中国湖北省，造成至少 15 人死亡。由于毁灭性风暴袭击该国，数十万人也被疏散。中国领导人习近平敦促“全力以赴”救援受灾群众

reflection.en: In the face of devastating natural disasters like the storms in Hubei, our hearts go out to those who have lost loved ones and homes. During such overwhelming times, we are reminded that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. May all affected find comfort and assistance, knowing they are not alone in their suffering.
reflection.zh: 面对像湖北风暴这样的毁灭性自然灾害，我们的心与那些失去亲人和家园的人同在。在这样令人不知所措的时刻，我们被提醒雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。愿所有受影响的人都能找到安慰和帮助，知道他们并非独自承受痛苦。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: China's missile test builds on Pacific nuclear deterrence
title.zh: 中国导弹试验增强太平洋核威慑

summary.en: US allies in the Pacific have condemned China's recent intercontinental ballistic missile test, which Beijing described as routine. The test is seen as a demonstration of China's increasing military capabilities.
summary.zh: 太平洋地区的美国盟友谴责了中国最近进行的洲际弹道导弹试验，北京称之为“例行”测试。此次试验被视为中国展示其日益增长的军事能力。

body.en:
US allies in the Pacific condemned what Beijing has called a "routine" intercontinental ballistic missile test, which comes as China seeks to demonstrate its growing military capabilities.

On Monday, the Chinese Navy conducted a missile test in the South Pacific , with state media reporting that a nuclear submarine fired a missile carrying a dummy warhead into international waters.

The test quickly drew harsh criticism from US allies in the Pacific. Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the Chinese test was destabilizing for regional security. Japan called on China to reconsider its actions.

New Zealand said it does not want China to use the South Pacific as a testing ground for missiles. "We are deeply concerned about China's tests of nuclear-capable weapons in the South Pacific," Foreign Minister Winston Peters said in Wellington

During the Cold War, the US tested numerous nuclear weapons around the South Pacific's Bikini Atoll, which today is part of the Marshall Islands. Since World War II, the US has dominated the postwar security architecture in the Pacific region .

China's military buildup is now challenging this construct . Although official media have not released any details about the test, nationalist military experts are speculating on Chinese social media about how powerful the tested missile might have been.

"It is a submarine-launched intercontinental ballistic missile of the Julang (JL)-3 series," wrote Lieutenant Colonel Zhang Junshe a researcher with the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Naval Military Academic Research Institute.

The Julang-3, which means "Giant Wave-3" in English, is currently still under development.

It is said to have a maximum range of 12,000 kilometers (7,400 miles) and can carry multiple nuclear warheads. So far, three successful tests have been reported between 2018 and 2019.

"The target of this missile is not combat troops on the front lines, but strategic targets such as command centers, military bases, or energy infrastructure," Zhang wrote in his blog.

The "Giant Wave-3" is believed to have been launched from a Type 094 Jin-class nuclear-powered submarine. With a full crew of 120 sailors, the 135-meter-long submarine can sustain a submerged crew for at least 70 days. Currently, the Chinese Navy has six Type 094 submarines in service.

According to the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a Washington-based think tank, China operates an additional 59 nuclear-powered attack submarines in addition to the Jin-class submarines.

"Even if all other military weapons were to be put out of action, the Chinese submarine would still be fully capable of launching a nuclear counterstrike," Zhang wrote.

As early as September 2024, China had launched an intercontinental missile carrying a dummy warhead from the...
body.zh: 美国在太平洋的盟友谴责北京所谓的“例行”洲际弹道导弹试验，此次试验是在中国寻求展示其不断增长的军事能力之际进行的。 周一，中国海军在南太平洋进行了一次导弹试验，官方媒体报道称，一艘核潜艇向国际水域发射了一枚携带假弹头的导弹。 这次试验很快引起了美国太平洋盟友的严厉批评。澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤表示，中国的试验破坏了地区安全的稳定。日本呼吁中国重新考虑其行动。 新西兰表示不希望中国利用南太平洋作为导弹试验场。外交部长温斯顿·彼得斯在惠灵顿表示：“我们对中国在南太平洋进行核武器试验深感担忧” 冷战期间，美国在南太平洋比基尼环礁（今天是马绍尔群岛的一部分）周围测试了许多核武器。二战以来，美国一直主导着太平洋地区的战后安全架构。 中国的军力建设现在正在挑战这种结构。尽管官方媒体尚未公布有关此次测试的任何细节，但民族主义军事专家正在中国社交媒体上猜测测试的导弹的威力可能有多大。 中国人民解放军海军军事学术研究院研究员张军社中校写道：“这是巨狼（JL）-3系列潜射洲际弹道导弹。” Julang-3，英文意思是“Giant Wave-3”，目前仍在开发中。 据称其最大射程为12,000公里（7,400英里），可携带多枚核弹头。到目前为止，2018 年至 2019 年间已报告了三项成功的测试。 张在博客中写道：“这种导弹的目标不是前线的作战部队，而是指挥中心、军事基地或能源基础设施等战略目标。” 据信“巨浪3”是从一艘094型晋级核动力潜艇上发射的。这艘135米长的潜艇共有120名水手，可以让水下船员至少生存70天。目前，中国海军有6艘094型潜艇在役。 据华盛顿智库核威胁倡议组织称，除了晋级潜艇之外，中国还拥有59艘核动力攻击潜艇。 张写道：“即使所有其他军事武器都无法发挥作用，中国潜艇仍然完全有能力发动核反击。” 早在2024年9月，中国就从...发射了一枚携带假弹头的洲际导弹。

reflection.en: The news of missile tests highlights the ongoing global pursuit of security through military strength. Yet, the prophet Isaiah envisioned a future where nations would transform instruments of war into tools for peace, no longer training for conflict. This vision reminds us to pray for leaders to seek true security not in escalating arms, but in pathways of...
reflection.zh: 导弹试验的消息凸显了全球通过军事力量寻求安全的持续努力。然而，先知以赛亚曾预见一个未来，各国将把战争工具变为和平工具，不再为冲突而训练。这一愿景提醒我们为领袖祷告，愿他们不在军备竞赛中寻求真正的安全，而是在相互理解和裁军的道路上。

title.en: Japan, China coast guards square off near disputed islands
title.zh: 日本和中国海警在争议岛屿附近对峙

summary.en: Japanese and Chinese coast guard vessels confronted each other near the disputed Senkaku island chain, with both sides claiming they expelled the other. The incident comes amid rising tensions between Tokyo and Beijing.
summary.zh: 日本和中国海警船在有争议的尖阁列岛（中国称钓鱼岛）附近相互对峙，双方都声称驱逐了对方。此次事件发生在中日两国关系日益紧张之际。

body.en:
Japanese and Chinese coast guard vessels confronted each other near the disputed Senkaku island chain, with both sides claiming they expelled the other. The incident comes amid rising tensions between Tokyo and Beijing.

Japanese and Chinese coast guard vessels traded accusations on Tuesday after an encounter near the disputed Senkaku islands — also known as the Diaoyu islands in China — in the East China Sea.

Japan's coast guard said four Chinese vessels were operating near the islands, two of which entered what Tokyo considers its territorial waters.

The Chinese ships were approaching a Japanese fishing vessel in the area, according to Japan's coast guard.

The Japanese coast guard said it then "issued orders to leave ... successfully forcing the Chinese coast guard vessels to leave Japanese territorial waters by approximately 9:20 am (0020 GMT) today."

Tokyo described the Chinese vessels' actions as "a violation of international law."

In a separate statement, China's coast guard said that a Japanese fishing boat had "intruded into" its territorial waters and that its ships had taken "necessary measures to warn and expel it."

The statement said that the disputed island chain was "China's inherent territory," and that the Chinese coast guard urged the "Japanese side to immediately stop all rights-violation and provocative acts in relevant waters."

The uninhabited Senkaku island chain is administered by Japan but claimed by China.

Located between Taiwan and Japan's Okinawa island chain, the islands have long been a source of friction between Beijing and Tokyo. Interest in the area has been amplified by the possibility of oil and natural gas reserves beneath the East China Sea.

Chinese government vessels frequently operate near the islands, although approaches to Japanese fishing boats are comparatively rare. Chinese coast guard ships were last reported to have entered waters claimed by Japan on June 10.

The latest incident comes against a backdrop of  increasingly strained ties between the two countries .

In November 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said her country could come to Taiwan's aid militarily in the event of a Chinese invasion.

These comments drew heavy criticism from Beijing. Since November, Chinese officials have called on their citizens to avoid traveling to Japan and have banned Japanese entities from receiving Chinese exports, including rare earth minerals.

This incident reminds us of the constant effort required from all parties to de-escalate and seek pathways for peaceful coexistence, even amidst territorial disputes.

title.en: How do Australia's 'great deals' with its neighbours compare to China?
title.zh: 澳大利亚与邻国的“大交易”与中国相比如何？

summary.en: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is strengthening diplomatic and economic ties with Pacific island nations, a region where China has significant influence.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯正在加强与太平洋岛国的外交和经济关系，该地区是中国具有重要影响力的区域。

body.en:
Anthony Albanese is turning his attention to the Solomon Islands after securing Australia a major new defence agreement with Fiji, as he seeks to shore up support against the expansion of Chinese influence in the region.

Albanese and Fijian Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka formalised the Ocean of Peace Alliance alongside an updated Vuvale Union partnership during a ceremony in the Fijian capital Suva on Monday.

Albanese hailed the treaties, aimed at strengthening regional security amid intensifying strategic competition in the Pacific, as "one of the most significant endeavours Australia has undertaken with any country".

Fiji is one of Australia's closest Pacific security partners and has one of the region's largest militaries, making the agreement one of Canberra's most noteworthy in the Pacific.

The visit to Suva is part of a days-long diplomatic mission during which Albanese will meet with several regional leaders including Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale for a whistle-stop tour on Tuesday, with the focus on a new comprehensive treaty.

The leaders last week agreed to start talks on a treaty to "capture the two countries' joint ambition for the relationship".

This latest push from Albanese comes as China confirmed on Monday it successfully tested a submarine-launched ballistic missile carried by a strategic nuclear submarine in international waters in the Pacific Ocean.

The agreements with Fiji expand the two nations' long-standing security and development relationship and introduce a mutual defence commitment.

The new Ocean of Peace Alliance commits both countries to consult and respond to security developments that threaten the sovereignty, peace or stability of either nation.

"Each Party recognises that an armed attack on any of the Parties within the Pacific would be dangerous to each other's peace and security as well as the security of the Pacific, and declares that it would act to meet the common danger, in accordance with its domestic processes," the deal reads.

Australia will support the partnership with more than $1 billion in funding over the next decade, targeting transnational crime prevention and investing in education, healthcare, and infrastructure projects in Fiji.

Australia works with all 14 Pacific Island nations to varying degrees, and has major security agreements with Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Tuvalu and Nauru.

title.en: 'Destabilising': Australia criticises China after ballistic missile test launch in the Pacific

summary.en: Australia has criticized China following a ballistic missile test launch in the Pacific, describing the action as "destabilising." This test marks China's latest intercontinental ballistic missile launch in 2024.

body.en:
Australia and New Zealand have sounded the alarm after China confirmed it successfully tested a ballistic missile carried by a strategic nuclear submarine in international waters in the Pacific Ocean.

Chinese state media Xinhua reported that the testing is part of China's annual military exercise, and it had alerted relevant countries in advance, in accordance with international law.

Xinhua described the launch as a "routine arrangement" of China's annual military training and said it was not directed against any specific country or target.

This comes after Australia and Fiji signed a major defence alliance earlier in the day, committing each country to come to the other's aid in case either is attacked.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the Australian government had been advised in advance by China of the test.

"Australia has been clear with China that we regard this as destabilising to the region," she told reporters on Monday, moments before the launch was confirmed.

"This proposed test is in the context of a rapid military buildup by China, which is lacking in the transparency and reassurance as to intent that the region expects."

Wong said the test was "inconsistent" with Pacific leaders' requests for the ocean to be one "of peace".

"It appears that, despite our long-standing concerns about this type of activity, China carried out the test within hours of informing us," he said in a statement.

"The Pacific is an Ocean of Peace and we are deeply concerned by China's testing of nuclear-capable weapons into the South Pacific."

Japan's government said it had been notified of the missile launch and urged China to reconsider.

"We expressed our grave concern over the Chinese military's increased activity," Tokyo said, adding that Japan's Coast Guard had been notified on Sunday by Chinese authorities about falling space debris that could fall within Japan's exclusive economic zone.

Japan's Kyodo news agency on Monday reported, citing a Japanese government source, that the missile had landed outside Japan's EEZ.

China's elite Rocket Force fired a dummy warhead into the sea near French Polynesia in September 2024, its first long-range missile launch over international waters in more than 40 years.

body.en:
Opposition leader Angus Taylor has spoken out in defence of Liberal senator Sarah Henderson's decision to test whether or not she could contact triple zero during Wednesday's Telstra outage.

Sarah Henderson, the Opposition's communications spokesperson, made two calls to the triple zero network after the service was disrupted by the widespread outage that caused chaos across the country .

Making false calls to triple zero is a criminal offence with a maximum penalty of three years in prison, and Henderson's test calls have been criticised by Labor as irresponsible.

Australia's largest telecommunications company faced connectivity issues for a second day, as a separate issue prevented some users from contacting triple zero.

While major issues were largely resolved by Telstra at approximately mid-morning on Wednesday, some transport networks remain slow or at a standstill on Thursday.

Early on Thursday morning, the company said overnight work had reduced the separate triple zero error by about 90 per cent. On Thursday afternoon, it said it had "implemented a solution" that had addressed the issue, and customers could feel confident calling triple zero.

Taylor argued on Thursday that Henderson was doing her job as Coalition communications spokesperson and that her actions were not illegal.

"If [Communications Minister Anika Wells] hadn't been absent for seven hours, Sarah wouldn't have had to do these things," Taylor said.

"These actions were not illegal and they were made necessary by complete and utter failure from this minister and that should be the focus of the press, and it should be the focus of the nation."

The senator insisted she was within her rights to make the test calls on Thursday morning.

"I was simply, as the shadow minister for communications, making those initial calls to work out whether the ... system was actually operating," she told Sydney radio station 2GB.

"I accept the criticism, but what I will say is that I am in a unique position holding this government to account."

Industry Minister Tim Ayres said making the calls at a time when the emergency phone network was being impacted was reckless.

"I was absolutely shocked by that revelation. I just say to Australians, don't do what she did," he told ABC radio.

"It's utterly irresponsible. I just don't know why anybody would do that, but I'd certainly say nobody should follow her example."

summary.en: Australia and India have signed an agreement allowing Australia to export uranium to India. The deal specifies that the uranium is to be used solely for "peaceful purposes."

body.en:
Australia will export uranium to India under a new agreement signed today between Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as the leader of the world's most populous country continues his visit to Australia.

"Today we can confirm the signing of the administrative arrangement to export uranium to India for peaceful purposes under the 2015 Australia-India nuclear cooperative agreement," Albanese told reporters in Canberra.

The agreement "facilitates Australian uranium exports to India to help increase the share of non-fossil fuel power capacity, providing an additional market for the Australian resources sector".

The 2015 agreement allowed Australian companies to export uranium to India on a commercial basis, but India's possession of nuclear weapons butted against Australia's nuclear safeguards, which meant uranium could only be exported for peaceful purposes.

Calling India a "top-tier" security partner, Albanese announced a raft of pledges he said reflected their shared vision for a peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific, including the development of a Memorandum of Understanding on the provision of defence services, and the repatriation of remains held in cultural institutions both in India and Australia.

Among the new measures, Albanese announced a temporary space-tracking terminal on Cocos Keeling Islands will support India's Human Space Flight program, which aims to send humans into space by 2027.

Australia will also re-award permanent major project status for Project Ceres, a urea manufacturing development in Karratha in Western Australia — producing nitrogen-based fertilizer to address disruptions in the global supply chain by the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz.

Not many world leaders can sell out an arena during an international diplomatic visit.

But tens of thousands of members of the Indian diaspora throughout Australia are expected to make their way to Melbourne's Docklands Stadium on Thursday night for a glimpse of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Modi arrived in Australia on Wednesday for a three-day trip as part of the Australia-India Annual Leaders' Summit, where he will meet with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.

A group of supporters of the Khalistan movement gathered to protest Modi's visit, outside an event at Government House on Thursday.

The Khalistan movement broadly advocates for a separate homeland for Sikhs, and has faced suppression by the Indian government.

title.en: ABC, SBS questioned on Gaza coverage by Royal Commission on Antisemitism
title.zh: 皇家反犹太主义委员会对 ABC 和 SBS 的加沙报道提出质疑

summary.en: The public broadcasters answered questions about their coverage of the Middle East, antisemitism and social cohesion.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The ABC and SBS have defended their reporting on conflict in the Middle East at the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

Earlier on Thursday, antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal told the commission that there was a strongly held perception among the Jewish community that the ABC was presenting biased and inaccurate reporting about the Hamas-Israel war.

"I'm not in any way suggesting that they shouldn't cover the matters that they consider important, but there are also lots of important issues around the world," the special envoy to combat antisemitism told the inquiry.

"There are major famines, there are wars that we don't hear about at all in Africa."

ABC editorial director Gavin Fang disagreed with the assessment, arguing the ABC aimed to present news accurately and impartially and platform a range of voices.

"We seek to, where relevant, hear from affected parties on a variety of sides of the conflict," he told the inquiry.

"That means hearing from both Palestinians and from Israelis ... hearing from government sources and from non-government."

Segal said a separate oversight committee should be established to ensure the broadcaster followed its rules, arguing the ombudsman that each organisation has is not sufficiently independent.

Fang said another oversight body was not needed and it wasn't clear how it would interact with the ombudsman.

SBS's Ombudsman Amy Stockwell, who was the final representative to speak at Thursday's hearings, said she was confident the current system is working.

"SBS has had an ombudsman for 21 years, so it's been designed and tested and refined over that period," she said.

"I think this model of co-regulation where there is an internal media ombudsman who is separate from the content divisions, but also still part of that ecosystem so that the audience has a very strong voice within the organisation."

Both the ABC and SBS can refer matters externally to the Australian Communications and Media Authority, which is expected to appear before the inquiry next week.

Segal also took aim at SBS's use of death statistics from the Gaza Health Ministry, claiming the figures were "grossly inaccurate" and failed to distinguish between combatants and non-combatants.

While some news outlets refer to the health ministry as being "Hamas-run", SBS news and current affairs director Mandi Wicks said she was confident SBS's overall coverage provides adequate context.

title.en: 'Can't treat our way out': Why Australia's $271 billion health spend could miss the mark
title.zh: “无法通过治疗解决问题”：澳大利亚2710亿澳元的医疗支出为何可能达不到预期

summary.en: A major new report highlights that while Australians are living longer, the healthcare system is under pressure due to rising out-of-pocket costs and an increase in chronic diseases. The findings suggest that current spending models may not effectively address these growing challenges.
summary.zh: 一份新的重要报告指出，尽管澳大利亚人寿命延长，但不断上涨的自付费用和慢性疾病正给医疗系统带来巨大压力。报告表明，目前的医疗支出模式可能无法有效应对这些日益严峻的挑战。

body.en:
Australians are now spending the equivalent of $10,037 per person on health goods and services annually, which represents a significant increase over a decade, a new government report has found.

The Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) report, Australia's health 2026, estimates that $270.5 billion was spent on health in 2023-24, the latest year surveyed.

Adjusted for inflation, that is an increase from the $8,615 spent per person a decade prior. It includes spending by federal, state and territory governments, health insurance providers, individuals, and non-government sources.

The figures are derived from the government's latest annual snapshot, published on Thursday, which reveals the nation's well-being.

It also found that Australians are living longer, despite a recent decline in life expectancy during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic . Males born between 2022 and 2024 are expected to live to age 81.1, while females are expected to live to 85.1.
